deliverable.rule: a grid-wide sensitivity result requires some uniform criterion scorable at n=3 in all 5 ratios; otherwise the honest deliverable is the bounded negative result
why: mean_val_cer: 8/15 cells scorable (per-ratio n 100:0=0, 75:25=2, 50:50=3, 25:75=3, 0:100=0); no scorable cell at all at RV:MS 100:0, 0:100
worst_val_cer: 2/15 cells scorable (per-ratio n 100:0=0, 75:25=0, 50:50=1, 25:75=1, 0:100=0); no scorable cell at all at RV:MS 100:0, 75:25, 0:100

early_stopping.note: early stopping is driven by the MIXED metric, so on a truncated trajectory a uniform criterion whose argmin is the last observed epoch was still improving when training stopped: its selected epoch is a LOWER BOUND, and the epoch a uniform rule would really have chosen is unobservable from any committed artifact

checks.best_metric: the trajectory's value at that epoch reproduces training_state.best_metric (tolerance 1e-09)
checks.metric_key: the Slurm header's metric_for_best_model equals results.json training_state.best_metric_key
checks.selection: re-selecting the cell's own metric_for_best_model over the recovered trajectory reproduces results.json training_state.best_epoch
checks.step_contract: best_step == best_epoch × 326 (the fixed PACLIC step contract)

paper: PACLIC 2026 — Cross-Notation Transfer in Vedic OCR

retention.why: save_total_limit=2 kept at most two checkpoints per run and the v2 launcher purges checkpoints on success, so a divergent cell is scorable only if a checkpoint at its uniform-rule step both SURVIVED and belongs to the run whose predictions are committed; a checkpoint left over from a superseded attempt of the same cell is an orphan and is excluded
